generation.method: Deterministic hand-authored fictional records created from an original teaching specification; no external data, fitted distribution, scraped values, model output, incident record, benchmark row, real identifier, or competing-course asset was used.

rights.authorship_assertion: The project authors created every byte of the fixture data and metadata except the names of open formats and the linked CC0 legal instrument.
rights.course_code_and_copy: Not covered by this data dedication; governed by the repository and source-specific terms.

datasheet.purpose: A small offline fixture for purpose and risk classification, stakeholder analysis, data minimisation, subgroup error calculation, uncertainty wording, assurance cards, effective human authority, contestability, red teaming, incident response, and a governance go/no-go dossier.
datasheet.unit_of_observation: One fictional evaluation case authored solely for a pre-release tabletop exercise; case codes do not correspond to people.
datasheet.composition: Sixteen fictional evaluation rows, four fictional stakeholder signals, four red-team injections, and one fictional incident tabletop around one invented system and organisation.
datasheet.sensitive_attributes: None. access_path and language_context are artificial test dimensions and explicitly must not be interpreted as disability, diagnosis, ethnicity, nationality, migration status, language proficiency, or another protected or sensitive characteristic.
datasheet.label_generation: All fields, reference labels, scores, thresholds, actions, quotations, and failure patterns were manually selected for inspectable exercises and do not arise from a population, institution, model, intervention, causal mechanism, or measured construct.
datasheet.maintenance: Immutable. Any byte change requires a new fixture version, new hash, and new notice/provenance version.

known_artificialities: The evaluation set is tiny and deliberately gives the alternate access path more authored errors so learners can detect a subgroup signal by hand.
The 0.60 threshold, reviewer actions, workload limit, response time, and incident severity are fictional policy inputs, not validated controls or recommendations.
Stakeholder quotations, red-team scenarios, and the incident timeline are authored prompts rather than empirical accounts.
No row, score, label, explanation, decision, appeal, or incident can be connected to a real person or organisation.

regulatory_boundary.rule: A real analysis must identify the jurisdiction, regulated role, system purpose and use, affected population, operative official text or standard version, and verification date.
regulatory_boundary.non_claim: The fixture does not classify a real system or establish any duty, exemption, conformity, privacy basis, fairness finding, or legal conclusion.

non_claims: No claim about real people, institutions, systems, models, incidents, harms, benefits, outcomes, disparities, or effectiveness.

No claim of representativeness, statistical significance, causal identification, calibration, privacy compliance, legal authorization, accessibility, security, safety, fairness, or production readiness.
No authorization for prediction, profiling, ranking, triage, support allocation, discipline, admission, grading, employment, benefit, or other decision involving a real person.
No claim that a completed impact assessment, audit, card, red-team log, or governance dossier constitutes independent assurance or release approval.
